vault.title: Creating Icy Drones From Scratch
vault.subtitle: Four ways to conjure cold, otherworldly drones
vault.summary: Those dark, icy drones that conjure alien landscapes aren't about owning the right gear. It's how you use the tools you already have.
body: **FM is your friend.** Frequency modulation pushes shimmering upper harmonics into your reverb and sounds fantastic in the low registers. No dedicated FM synth? Vital and Serum can do “pseudo FM” between oscillators. Tame it with an envelope or LFO, because things get wild fast. Surge XT, Dune 3 and Phase Plant are great here too.

**Embrace modular.** Modular gives you true FM in many flavours and total control over what modulates what. VCV Rack (free), Voltage Modular, Softube Modular or real Eurorack all work. Keep experimenting with synthesis and modulation; you can even run audio into modulation inputs.

**Reverb for space.** Don't just max out size and decay and let the reverb do everything. Keep size and decay high, but start with the mix around 25–50%. The drone's natural harmonics come through, and the reverb carries on where the synth leaves off.
**Don't forget the bass.** A slow-moving bass layer gives your drone a foundation the listener can feel. Pair it with an icy pad drone and the effect is far more dramatic than either on its own.

vault.title: Texture Loom 1.5
vault.subtitle: A free dual-source granular instrument
vault.summary: Load two samples and weave them into evolving pads, drones, cinematic beds and playable clouds. For macOS (AU/VST3) and Windows (VST3).
body: Each source can play back conventionally or as a cloud of grains, with control over grain size, density, spray, stereo width and pitch jitter.
Eight-voice polyphony, two Motion generators and a modulation matrix with up to 16 routes keep your textures moving.
Two multimode filters, an equal-power blend between the sources and a built-in reverb shape the space. An updated 26-page manual is included.
